claims.text: Only 7% of reviewed medical text summarization studies conducted external validation.
Only 3% of reviewed medical text summarization studies performed patient safety assessments.
Hallucination rates in medical text summarization using LLMs range from 1.47% to 61.6%.
Existing reporting guidelines do not adequately address the specific requirements of medical text summarization tasks.
The final MEDAI-LLM-SUMM checklist comprises 24 items organized into six sections.
MEDAI-LLM-SUMM uniquely addresses hallucination assessment requirements compared to six existing reporting standards.
MEDAI-LLM-SUMM uniquely addresses reference summary creation methodology compared to six existing reporting standards.
MEDAI-LLM-SUMM uniquely addresses LLM-as-judge validation protocols compared to six existing reporting standards.
MEDAI-LLM-SUMM uniquely addresses detailed pilot testing specifications compared to six existing reporting standards.

methodologies.name: Modified iterative consensus approach
methodologies.description: A three-stage process involving systematic literature review, initial checklist development, and consensus discussions among a multidisciplinary expert panel.

limitations.text: Existing reporting guidelines, including CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, TRIPOD-LLM, and DEAL, do not adequately address the specific requirements of medical text summarization tasks.
Critical gaps persist in safety validation, evaluation frameworks, and clinical deployment readiness, with only 7% conducting external validation and 3% performing patient safety assessments.
